source: IOK Arabic — Ṣarf section, class notes to 2026-09-08

cards.front: What is صَرْف?
cards.back: Arabic morphology — the science that gives us the words themselves; نَحْو then tells us what to do with them

cards.front: What are the two components of a verb?
cards.back: The فِعْل (the verb itself) and the ضَمِير (the pronoun)

cards.meaning: the pronoun — the person, gender, and number of the one carrying out the action
third person
second person
first person

cards.text: Person: third is {{c1::غَائِب}}, second is {{c2::مُخَاطَب}}, first is {{c3::مُتَكَلِّم}}

cards.meaning: masculine
feminine

cards.front: What are the two terms for singular?
What are the two terms for dual?
What are the two terms for plural?
What does مُفْرَد mean in صَرْف, and how does that differ from its use in نَحْو?
cards.back: In صَرْف it means singular (number); in نَحْو it means a single word (= كَلِمَة)

cards.meaning: an attached pronoun
a separated, standalone pronoun

cards.text: An attached pronoun is a {{c1::ضَمِير مُتَّصِل}}; a separated one is a {{c2::ضَمِير مُنْفَصِل}}

cards.meaning: the pronoun in its role as doer of the action — one category of attached pronoun
a hidden pronoun — contained within the verb, not written
a visible pronoun — attached to the verb as a suffix

cards.text: The {{c1::مُسْتَتِر::hidden}} pronoun sits inside the verb; the {{c2::بَارِز::visible}} pronoun is attached as a suffix

cards.front: Under which category of attached pronoun do مُسْتَتِر and بَارِز fall?
cards.back: ضَمِير الفَاعِل — the pronoun as doer

cards.meaning: each form of the verb taken with a particular pronoun

cards.front: How many صِيَغ are there in a full conjugation?
In which two صِيَغ is the pronoun مُسْتَتِر?
Why is the pronoun in هُوَ counted as مُسْتَتِر?
cards.back: Because nothing is added to the verb at all

cards.front: A تاء is added in هِيَ — so why is its pronoun still counted as مُسْتَتِر?
cards.back: Because that تاء ساكنة is a عَلَامَة التَّأْنِيث, a sign of femininity, not a ضَمِير

cards.meaning: a sign of femininity — not a pronoun

cards.front: How does the third person feminine dual differ from the feminine singular in what it adds?
cards.back: It keeps the تاء as a sign of femininity and adds the pronoun أَلِف on top of it

cards.front: Which parts of a conjugated verb count as ضَمِير بَارِز?
cards.back: The added suffixes — أَلِف, وَاو, نُون, and the rest

cards.text: Within a person, feminine singular is marked by {{c1::ـَة}}, the dual by {{c2::ـَانِ / ـَتَانِ}}, masculine plural by {{c3::ـُونَ}}, feminine plural by {{c4::ـَات}}
cards.extra: Read off the ṣiyagh chart; not stated in the lecture.

cards.text: {{c1::المُتَكَلِّمُونَ}} — {{c2::first person, dual or plural, masculine or feminine — “we”}}

cards.front: Which person makes no gender distinction?
cards.back: The first — المُتَكَلِّم and المُتَكَلِّمُونَ each cover both

cards.front: Which صِيغَة covers both dual and plural?
What does فَتَحَ mean?
Which two صِيَغ share an identical مَاضِي form?

cards.meaning: the past tense

cards.front: Which four مَاضِي forms end in a تاء and are indistinguishable without tashkīl?

cards.text: Written bare, all four are فعلت: {{c1::فَعَلَتْ::sukūn}} is she; {{c2::فَعَلْتَ::fatḥah}} is you (m/s); {{c3::فَعَلْتِ::kasrah}} is you (f/s); {{c4::فَعَلْتُ::ḍammah}} is I
cards.extra: The vowel on the تاء is the only thing carrying person and gender here.

cards.front: When a وَاو pronoun is the last letter of a word, what always follows it?
cards.back: A silent أَلِف — as in فَتَحُوْا

cards.front: Which two tenses does المُضَارِع cover?

cards.meaning: the present tense
the future tense

cards.text: الحَال has two types: {{c1::present habitual::regularly}} — “Zaid walks” — and {{c2::present continuous::right now}} — “Zaid is walking”

cards.front: What does the present habitual express?
cards.back: An action that takes place regularly — “Zaid walks”

cards.front: What does the present continuous express?
cards.back: An action taking place right now — “Zaid is walking”

cards.text: Each صِيغَة has four components: {{c1::الفِعْل::the verb}}, {{c2::الضَّمِير::the pronoun}}, {{c3::حَرْف المُضَارِع::the prefix}}, and {{c4::عَلَامَة الإِعْرَاب::the state marker}}

cards.meaning: the مُضَارِع prefix — also called عَلَامَة المُضَارِع

cards.front: What is the other name for حَرْف المُضَارِع?

cards.meaning: a letter or ḥarakah which indicates the grammatical state

cards.text: Breaking down يَفْتَحُوْنَ: {{c1::يَ::prefix}} is the حَرْف المُضَارِع, {{c2::فْتَحُ::verb}} is the فِعْل, {{c3::وْ::pronoun}} is the ضَمِير, and {{c4::نَ::marker}} is the عَلَامَة الإِعْرَاب
المُضَارِع of فَتَحَ — الغَائِبُ — {{c1::يَفْتَحُ}} — ({{c2::هُوَ}}) — “he opens / is opening / will open”

cards.front: How many مُضَارِع conjugations carry no pronoun suffix, and which are they?
cards.back: Five — هُوَ، هِيَ، أَنْتَ، أَنَا، نَحْنُ

cards.front: What term do the notes give for the five conjugations with no suffix?
cards.back: الأَفْعَال الخَمْسَة (see draft — this label conventionally names the five نُون-ending forms instead)

cards.meaning: the نُون of the two feminine plurals — it counts as the ضَمِير itself
the نُون that marks the grammatical state at the end of a مُضَارِع conjugation

cards.text: {{c1::نُون النِّسْوَة}} is the ضَمِير itself and those two conjugations have {{c2::no عَلَامَة إِعْرَاب at all}}; {{c3::نُون الإِعْرَاب}} is what the remaining conjugations end with
cards.extra: Two different nūns at the end of a verb — this is the pair to keep apart.

cards.front: Which two conjugations carry نُون النِّسْوَة?
cards.back: The two feminine plurals — الغَائِبَاتُ (يَفْتَحْنَ) and المُخَاطَبَاتُ (تَفْتَحْنَ)

cards.front: What is a وَزْن, generically?
cards.back: The pattern of a word when placed on فَ عَيْن لَام

cards.front: Which words can be put on the وَزْن pattern?

cards.meaning: the categories verbs are divided into, by the vowel combinations of the عَيْن الكَلِمَة

cards.front: On what basis are verbs of family one divided into أَبْوَاب?
cards.back: The combinations of the vowel on the عَيْن الكَلِمَة

cards.meaning: family one — the هُوَ form carries no extra letter
families two and above — the هُوَ form does carry extra letters

cards.text: {{c1::ثُلَاثِي مُجَرَّد}} — the هُوَ form has {{c2::no extra letter}}; {{c3::ثُلَاثِي مَزِيد فِيه}} — the هُوَ form {{c4::does have extra letters}}

cards.front: To what does بَاب refer, across the families?
cards.back: To families two and above, and also to the sub-combinations within family one

cards.text: The six أَبْوَاب of ثُلَاثِي مُجَرَّد, in order of commonality: (1) {{c1::نَصَرَ يَنْصُرُ}} (2) {{c2::ضَرَبَ يَضْرِبُ}} (3) {{c3::فَتَحَ يَفْتَحُ}} (4) {{c4::سَمِعَ يَسْمَعُ}} (5) {{c5::كَرُمَ يَكْرُمُ}} (6) {{c6::حَسِبَ يَحْسِبُ}}
cards.extra: This order has to be memorised.

cards.front: Which بَاب is the most common?
Which بَاب is the least common of the six?
Which بَاب has the vowel pattern fatḥah → ḍammah on the عَيْن?
cards.back: نَصَرَ يَنْصُرُ — number 1 in order of commonality

cards.front: Which بَاب has the vowel pattern fatḥah → kasrah on the عَيْن?
cards.back: ضَرَبَ يَضْرِبُ — number 2 in order of commonality

cards.front: Which بَاب has the vowel pattern fatḥah → fatḥah on the عَيْن?
cards.back: فَتَحَ يَفْتَحُ — number 3 in order of commonality

cards.front: Which بَاب has the vowel pattern kasrah → fatḥah on the عَيْن?
cards.back: سَمِعَ يَسْمَعُ — number 4 in order of commonality

cards.front: Which بَاب has the vowel pattern ḍammah → ḍammah on the عَيْن?
cards.back: كَرُمَ يَكْرُمُ — number 5 in order of commonality

cards.front: Which بَاب has the vowel pattern kasrah → kasrah on the عَيْن?
cards.back: حَسِبَ يَحْسِبُ — number 6 in order of commonality

cards.front: Of the nine possible mādī–muḍāriʿ vowel combinations, how many actually occur?
Which three vowel combinations do not occur?
Which is the only بَاب whose مَاضِي carries a ḍammah on the عَيْن?

cards.text: {{c1::<bdi>الوَزْن</bdi>}} is the pattern; {{c2::<bdi>الصِّيغَة</bdi>}} is the actual entry on the table
cards.extra: Two words for two different things — the shape, and the filled-in form.

cards.front: How many voices does a verb have, and what are they?
What makes a verb active, and what is it called?
cards.back: The <bdi>فَاعِل</bdi> is mentioned — <bdi>فِعْلٌ مَعْلُومٌ فَاعِلُهُ</bdi>, or just <bdi>مَعْلُوم</bdi>

cards.front: What makes a verb passive, and what is it called?
cards.back: The subject is not mentioned and the verb is attributed to the direct object — <bdi>فِعْلٌ مَجْهُولٌ فَاعِلُهُ</bdi>, or just <bdi>مَجْهُول</bdi>

cards.meaning: the active voice — literally, the one whose doer is known
the passive voice — literally, the one whose doer is unknown

cards.text: Forming the past passive, for all forms: {{c1::leave the last letter as it is}}; {{c2::change the penultimate letter to a kasrah}}; {{c3::change every remaining vowelled letter to a ḍammah — a sukūn stays a sukūn}}
Forming the present passive, for all forms: {{c1::change the first letter to a ḍammah}}; {{c2::give the penultimate a fatḥah}}; {{c3::leave every other letter alone}}
In the past passive the penultimate takes a {{c1::kasrah}}; in the present passive it takes a {{c2::fatḥah}}
cards.extra: The penultimate letter is where the two rules differ.

cards.front: Which verb forms already begin with a ḍammah, so the present-passive rule changes nothing there?
Which verb forms already carry a fatḥah on the penultimate letter?

cards.text: {{c1::All}} <bdi>أَسْمَاء</bdi> have <bdi>إِعْرَاب</bdi>; {{c2::no}} <bdi>حُرُوف</bdi> do; and {{c3::some but not all}} <bdi>أَفْعَال</bdi> do

cards.meaning: a word whose ending does not change — it has no <bdi>إِعْرَاب</bdi>
a word whose ending changes with its grammatical state

cards.text: {{c1::<bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi>}}: the <bdi>حُرُوف</bdi> and the <bdi>فِعْل مَاضِي</bdi>. {{c2::<bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi>}}: the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> and the <bdi>أَسْمَاء</bdi>

cards.front: Which tense of the verb is <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi>?

cards.text: The three states of the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>: {{c1::<bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi> — the default}}; {{c2::<bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi> — after a <bdi>حَرْف نَاصِب</bdi>}}; {{c3::<bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi> — after a <bdi>حَرْف جَازِم</bdi>}}

cards.front: Which state is the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> in by default?
What puts a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> into <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>?
What puts a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> into <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>?
In how many ways do the 14 <bdi>صِيَغ</bdi> express their state?
cards.back: Three — the conjugations fall into three categories

cards.text: Category 1 — the five with no suffix: the <bdi>لَام الكَلِمَة</bdi> takes a {{c1::ḍammah}} when <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>, a {{c2::fatḥah}} when <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>, and a {{c3::sukūn}} when <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>

cards.front: What happens to the two feminine plurals across the three states?
cards.back: Nothing — they do not change, and are in fact considered <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi>

cards.front: What happens to the conjugations ending in <bdi>نُون الإِعْرَاب</bdi> when they leave <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>?
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the past passive, <bdi>هُمَا</bdi> (m).
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the past passive, <bdi>هُوَ</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the past passive, <bdi>هِيَ</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُوَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present passive, <bdi>هُوَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُوَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>.
cards.back: يَفْتَحَ (no suffix, so the لَام takes a fatḥah)

cards.front: From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُوَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>.
cards.back: يَفْتَحْ (no suffix, so the لَام takes a sukūn)

cards.front: From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present passive, <bdi>هُوَ</bdi>, <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُمَا</bdi> (m), <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُمَا</bdi> (m), <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُمْ</bdi>, <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُمْ</bdi>, <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>هُنَّ</bdi>, <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>.
From <bdi>فَتَحَ</bdi> — give the present active, <bdi>أَنَا</bdi>, <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>.
Apply the past-passive rule to <bdi>كَتَبَ</bdi>.
Apply the present-passive rule to <bdi>يَكْتُبُ</bdi>.

cards.meaning: an affirmative verb — the action did take place
a negated verb — the action did not take place

cards.front: How is the <bdi>مَاضِي</bdi> negated, and is that particle <bdi>عَامِل</bdi>?
cards.back: By putting <bdi>مَا</bdi> at the beginning — and it is <bdi>غَيْر عَامِل</bdi>

cards.front: Which four particles negate the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>?

cards.text: Negating the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> — time: {{c1::<bdi>لَمْ</bdi>}} gives a past meaning, {{c2::<bdi>لَا</bdi>}} a future meaning, and {{c3::<bdi>لَنْ</bdi>}} an emphatic future negation
Negating the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> — <bdi>عَمَل</bdi>: {{c1::<bdi>لَمْ</bdi> and <bdi>لَنْ</bdi>}} are <bdi>عَامِل</bdi>; {{c2::<bdi>مَا</bdi> and <bdi>لَا</bdi>}} are <bdi>غَيْر عَامِل</bdi>
cards.extra: Two of the four change the state of the verb after them.

cards.front: What does <bdi>لَمْ</bdi> do to the meaning of a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>?
What distinguishes <bdi>لَنْ</bdi> from <bdi>لَا</bdi>?
cards.back: Both negate the future, but <bdi>لَنْ</bdi> is emphatic

cards.front: Which states do <bdi>لَمْ</bdi> and <bdi>لَنْ</bdi> put the verb into?
cards.back: <bdi>لَمْ</bdi> is a <bdi>حَرْف جَازِم</bdi> → <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>; <bdi>لَنْ</bdi> is a <bdi>حَرْف نَاصِب</bdi> → <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>. Your notes say only that both are <bdi>عَامِل</bdi> — this pairing is not stated.
